## Introduction: Deer Observation Data and Methods

This section presents exploratory patterns in white-tailed deer observations across North Carolina from 2010 to 2020.
The dataset contains 2,891 iNaturalist observation records, including observation dates, geographic coordinates, and quality indicators.

We calculated the annual observation data to analyze the temporal trends.
Additionally, to study the spatial distribution, we used spatial connection technology to match the observation coordinates with the boundary polygons of each county in North Carolina, and summarized and visualized the county-level data.
The analysis focuses on recorded observations rather than the actual abundance of deer.

## Research Question
Are white-tailed deer observations more frequent at a close distance to developed areas that border wildland vegetation in North Carolina?

## Intended Audience 
As white-tailed deer populations in North Carolina increase due to few natural predators, and population growth during off-hunting seasons, human-deer conflicts can become more prevalent. This sometimes mean an increase in vehical collisions. Knowing the number of deer and distance they are away from developed areas bordering wildland vegetation can inform the North Carolina Wildlife Resource Commission on region specific harvest strategies. It can also help land owners and land conservation organizations understand where to watch for deer presence in their neighborhoods and on protected lands.

## Figures and Maps

### Deer Observations in NC and Related iNaturalist Users

```{r counting observations by year, include = FALSE}
# Count deer observations by year
annual_counts <- as.data.frame(
  table(df_deer_clean$year)
)

# Rename columns
names(annual_counts) <- c("Year", "Observations")

# Convert year and count to numeric
annual_counts$Year <- as.integer(
  as.character(annual_counts$Year)
)

annual_counts$Observations <- as.integer(
  annual_counts$Observations
)

# View the summary table
annual_counts

```
```{r observer_data, include=FALSE}
# Load raw iNaturalist data
df_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/raw/NC_WhiteTailedDeer_iNaturalist_public.csv"
)

# Keep only observations in the cleaned dataset
df_users <- df_raw[
  df_raw$id %in% df_deer_clean$id,
]

# Count unique observers per year
unique_users <- aggregate(
  user_id ~ year,
  data = transform(
    df_users,
    year = as.integer(
      format(as.Date(observed_on), "%Y")
    )
  ),
  FUN = function(x) length(unique(x[!is.na(x)]))
)

names(unique_users) <- c("Year", "Unique_Observers")

# Combine annual observations with observer counts
annual_comparison <- merge(
  annual_counts,
  unique_users,
  by = "Year"
)
```

```{r year_slider, echo=FALSE}
sliderInput(
  inputId = "year_range",
  label = "Select Year:",

  max = 2020,

)
```



```{r interactive_annual_plot, echo=FALSE}
renderPlot({

  annual_filtered <- annual_comparison |>
    dplyr::filter(
      Year >= 2010,
      Year <= input$year_range
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(Year)

  plot(
    annual_filtered$Year,
    annual_filtered$Observations,
    type = "o",
    pch = 16,
    col = "steelblue",
    lwd = 2,
    xlab = "Year",
    ylab = "Number of observations / unique observers",
    xaxt = "n",
    xlim = c(2010, 2020),
    ylim = c(0, max(
      annual_comparison$Observations,
      annual_comparison$Unique_Observers
    ))
  )

  axis(1, at = 2010:2020)

  lines(
    annual_filtered$Year,
    annual_filtered$Unique_Observers,
    type = "o",
    pch = 17,
    col = "darkorange",
    lwd = 2
  )

  legend(
    "topleft",
    legend = c("Deer observations", "Unique iNaturalist observers"),
    col = c("steelblue", "darkorange"),
    pch = c(16, 17),
    lty = 1,
    bty = "n"
  )

})
```

### Correlation between Housing Unit Difference (HU_dif) and Vegetation Coverage Difference (VC_dif)

The following map shows that counties with larger increases in housing units generally experienced greater decreases in vegetation coverage. 

```{r, echo= FALSE}
map1_deer_in_NC = ggplot() + 
  geom_sf(data = NC_map, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, aes(fill = HU_dif)) + 
  scale_fill_gradient(low="darkblue", high="red") +
  labs(title = "Housing Unit (HU) and Vegetation Coverage (VC) Difference by Counties in NC",
       fill = "HU Difference") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11))

map2_deer_in_NC = ggplot() + 
  geom_sf(data = NC_map, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, aes(fill = VEG_dif)) + 
  scale_fill_gradient(low="yellow",high="#062D03") +
  labs(fill = "VC Difference",) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, vjust = -2, size = 12),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11))

map1_deer_in_NC / map2_deer_in_NC
```

#### Diagnostic plots for Correlation
```{r, include=FALSE}
model <- lm(VEG_dif ~ HU_dif, data = NC_map)
summary(model)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
res_cor <- model$res
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(x = NC_map$HU_dif,  y = NC_map$VEG_dif,
  main = "HU_dif vs. VEG_dif",
  xlab = "HU_dif",
  ylab = "VEG_dif",
  pch = 19,
  col = "steelblue")
abline(lm(VEG_dif ~ HU_dif, data = NC_map), col = "red", lwd = 2)
qqnorm(res_cor, datax = TRUE)
qqline(res_cor, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```

#### Key Summary of the Correlation Test

1. Significant correlation between HU_dif and VC_dif (p < 2e-16).

2. Equation: VC_dif = 143.34756 - 0.65957(HU_dif)

3. Strong negative correlation between the two variables (R = - 0.9264973).

4. 85.7% of the VC_dif variance is explained by HU_dif.


```{r, include = FALSE}

# Convert deer coordinates into spatial points
deer_sf <- st_as_sf(
  df_deer_clean,
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
  crs = 4326,
  remove = FALSE
)

# Match the coordinate system of the county map
deer_sf <- st_transform(deer_sf, st_crs(NC_map))

# Assign each deer observation to a county
deer_county <- st_join(
  deer_sf,
  NC_map[, c("NAME", "GEOID")],
  join = st_within,
  left = TRUE
)


# Preview the results
head(st_drop_geometry(deer_county)[, c("id", "NAME", "GEOID")])
```

### Map Comparisons with Deer Observation

```{r plot_function, echo= FALSE}
plot_it <- function(the_parameter) {

  # Filter deer observations by year
  deer_before <- deer_sf |>
    filter(year >= 2010, year <= 2015)

  deer_after <- deer_sf |>
    filter(year == 2020)

  # Set legend title based on selected variable
  legend_title <- if (the_parameter == "HU_dif") {
    "Housing Unit Difference"
  } else {
    "Vegetation Difference"
  }
  
  if (the_parameter == "HU_dif") {
  my_low  <- "darkblue"
  my_high <- "red"
} else {
  my_low  <- "yellow"
  my_high <- "#062D03"
}

  # Map 1: 2010–2015
  map_before <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(
      data = NC_map,
      aes(fill = .data[[the_parameter]]),
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_sf(
      data = deer_before,
      aes(color = "Deer Observations"),
      size = 0.5,
      alpha = 0.5,
      stroke = 0.5
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = my_low, high = my_high) +
    scale_color_manual(
      name = NULL,
      values = c("Deer Observations" = "cyan"),
      guide = guide_legend(
        override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1)
      )
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Deer Observations (2010–2015)",
      fill = legend_title
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11.5)
    )

  # Map 2: 2020
  map_after <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(
      data = NC_map,
      aes(fill = .data[[the_parameter]]),
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_sf(
      data = deer_after,
      aes(color = "Deer Observations"),
      size = 0.5,
      alpha = 0.5,
      stroke = 0.5
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = my_low, high = my_high) +
    scale_color_manual(
      name = NULL,
      values = c("Deer Observations" = "cyan"),
      guide = guide_legend(
        override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1)
      )
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Deer Observations (2020)",
      fill = legend_title
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11.5)
    )

  # Stack maps vertically with one shared legend
patchwork::wrap_plots(
  map_before,
  map_after,
  ncol = 1
)
}
```


```{r interactive_map, echo=FALSE}
selectInput(
  inputId = "the_parameter",
  label = "Select Land Use Variable:",
  choices = c(
    "Housing Difference" = "HU_dif",
    "Vegetation Difference" = "VEG_dif"
  ),
  selected = "HU_dif"
)

# Display both maps
renderPlot({

  plot_it(input$the_parameter)

}, height = 850)

```
In terms of housing units, the deer observations before the development (2010-2015) spread out more than the once from 2020, which gather in 4 clusters in the counties with more housing units. For vegetation cover changes, the pattern is less obvious: deer observations cluster in both regions with high and low vegetation loss.

## ANOVA Results
```{r, include - FALSE}
df_deer_spatial <- df_deer_clean %>%
  select(observed_on, year, longitude, latitude) %>%
  mutate(year = as.character(year)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c('longitude','latitude'), crs=4269)
```

```{r data wrangling, include = FALSE}
df_deer_in_NC <- st_join(df_deer_spatial, NC_map, join = st_within) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  filter(year != "2016" & year != "2017" & year != "2018" & year != "2019") %>%
  mutate(development = ifelse(HU_dif > 0, "yes", "no"),
         forest = ifelse(VEG_dif < 0, "dec", "inc"),
         year = ifelse(year == "2020", "2020", "20102015")) %>%
  group_by(NAME, year, development, forest) %>%
  summarise(observation=n()) %>%
  ungroup(year, development, forest) %>%
  mutate(period = ifelse(year == "2020", "after", "before"))
```

```{r ANOVA Development, include = FALSE}
model_dev <- aov(log(observation) ~ period + development + period*development, data = df_deer_in_NC)
summary(model_dev)
TukeyHSD(model_dev)
cld_dev <- multcompLetters4(model_dev, TukeyHSD(model_dev))
print(cld_dev)
```

```{r ANOVA Development Validity, include = FALSE}
fit_dev <- model_dev$fitted
res_dev <- model_dev$res

par(mfrow=c(2,2))
boxplot(observation ~ development+period, data = df_deer_in_NC)
qqnorm(res_dev, datax = TRUE)
qqline(res_dev, col = "red", lwd = 2)
plot(x = seq(1:length(res_dev)), y = res_dev, xlab="Order", ylab="Residuals")
lines(x = seq(1:length(res_dev)), y = res_dev)
abline(0,0)
plot(fit_dev, res_dev, xlab="Fitted Values", ylab="Residuals")
```

```{r ANOVA Forest, include = FALSE}
model_forest <- aov(log(observation) ~ period + forest + period*forest, data = df_deer_in_NC)
summary(model_forest)
TukeyHSD(model_forest)
cld_forest <- multcompLetters4(model_forest, TukeyHSD(model_forest))
print(cld_forest)
```

```{r ANOVA Forest Validity, include = FALSE}
fit_forest <- model_forest$fitted
res_forest <- model_forest$res

par(mfrow=c(2,2))
boxplot(observation ~ forest+period, data = df_deer_in_NC)
qqnorm(res_forest, datax = TRUE)
qqline(res_forest, col = "red", lwd = 2)
plot(x = seq(1:length(res_forest)), y = res_forest, xlab="Order", ylab="Residuals")
lines(x = seq(1:length(res_forest)), y = res_forest)
abline(0,0)
plot(fit_forest, res_forest, xlab="Fitted Values", ylab="Residuals")
```

The following table summarizes the effects of observation period, land-use change, and their interaction on log-transformed deer observation counts.
## ANOVA Model Diagnostics

Select a model to examine its diagnostic plots.

```{r interactive_anova_validity, echo=FALSE}

# Select ANOVA model
selectInput(
  inputId = "anova_validity",
  label = "Select ANOVA Model:",
  choices = c(
    "Housing Development" = "development",
    "Vegetation Change" = "forest"
  ),
  selected = "forest"
)

# Display selected diagnostic plots
renderPlot({

  if (input$anova_validity == "development") {
    model <- model_dev
    variable <- "development"
  } else {
    model <- model_forest
    variable <- "forest"
  }

  # Extract fitted values and residuals
  fit <- fitted(model)
  res <- residuals(model)

  # Arrange plots in 2x2 layout
  par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

  # 1. Boxplot
  boxplot(
    as.formula(paste("observation ~", variable, "+ period")),
    data = df_deer_in_NC,
    main = "Deer Observations by Group",
    xlab = "Group",
    ylab = "Observations",
    outline = FALSE
  )

  # 2. Normal Q-Q plot
  qqnorm(
    res,
    main = "Normal Q-Q Plot"
  )
  qqline(res, col = "red", lwd = 2)

  # 3. Residuals by observation order
  plot(
    seq_along(res), res,
    xlab = "Observation Order",
    ylab = "Residuals",
    main = "Residuals by Order"
  )
  lines(seq_along(res), res)
  abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)

  # 4. Residuals vs fitted values
  plot(
    fit, res,
    xlab = "Fitted Values",
    ylab = "Residuals",
    main = "Residuals vs Fitted"
  )
  abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)

}, height = 700)
```

```{r interactive_anova, echo=FALSE}

# Select which ANOVA to display
selectInput(
  inputId = "anova_selection",
  label = "Select ANOVA Model:",
  choices = c(
    "Housing Development" = "development",
    "Vegetation Change" = "forest"
  ),
  selected = "development"
)

# Display selected ANOVA table
renderTable({

  if (input$anova_selection == "development") {
    model <- model_dev
  } else {
    model <- model_forest
  }

  as.data.frame(summary(model)[[1]]) |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Variable")

}, digits = 4, rownames = FALSE)

```
We marked the deer observations from 2010-2015 as pre-development and the data from 2020 as post-development. We also marked the different levels of development and vegetation coverage based on the subtraction columns.
development: no value <= 0; yes value > 0
vegetation coverage: inc value > 0; dec value < 0
To fit the ANOVA assumptions better, according to the validity plots, the data is natural log transformed, and the assumptions are fulfilled, showing in the diagnosis plots.  
For housing units, development and period are both significant on deer observation. The Tukey test shows that the counties that have significant difference of deer observations before and after development are those with development.
For vegetation cover, forest clearing and period are both significant on deer observation. The Tukey test shows that the counties that have significant difference of deer observations before and after development are those with vegetation coverage decline.
